title: Washington Ethics Advisory Opinion 26-03
text:
Opinion 26-03 (Amended)
Questions:
Our court maintains a list of all judges who perform weddings and lists them by location with their contact information. The list also indicates whether a judge refers to be contacted by text message or phone call. We are aware of Ethics Advisory Opinion 20-01 but have a very specific question. On our list, is it appropriate to list other languages the judges speak, as a service to the public? We find that language assistance plan individuals have to call multiple judges in multiple jurisdictions to find one that can perform a ceremony in their native language.
Answer:
Judicial officers should promote public confidence in the independence, integrity, and impartiality of the judiciary, and avoid impropriety or the appearance of impropriety. CJC Rule 1.2. Judicial officers should also avoid abusing the prestige of office for personal gain. CJC Rule 1.3.
Courts can maintain a list of judicial officers who perform wedding services that provide general information about those services, but the list should not draw the
public's attention to the uniqueness of any individual judicial officer's services. EAO 20-01. In the example provided in the query, the current list includes each judge's name, their location, and contact information. No other information is currently provided on the court's list.
Ethics Advisory Opinion 20-01 recognized that judges may wish to provide additional information, such as whether a judge can perform services in a language other than English. The Committee stated that listing additional specific services "not tied to any specific judicial officer is acceptable." EAO 20-01. However, "[w]hile the additional information can be considered as simply information on the court's website, it may also serve the purpose of drawing the public's attention to the uniqueness of the individual judge to promote the sale of that judge's service of performing a wedding ceremony for a fee." Id. Promoting the sale of a particular judge's service of performing a wedding ceremony for a fee would run afoul of the rule requiring judges to avoid abusing the prestige of office for personal gain. CJC Rule 1.3. This rule was again recognized in EAO 23-04, which concluded that it is acceptable to post a statement that, "judges who officiate weddings, do so without bias, prejudice, or discrimination," if the statement is not attributed to a particular judicial officer.
Because the languages a judge speaks are attributable to a particular judge, listing the languages draws attention to the uniqueness of that judge, promoting the sale of that judge's service over others. Therefore, including the languages a judge speaks on the list when that judge charges and collects money for performing wedding ceremonies would give the appearance of impropriety and abuse the prestige of judicial office to advance the economic interest of the judge and should be avoided.
However, consistent with EAO 20-01, listing the languages in which wedding ceremonies may be conducted - without attributing those languages to any specific
judicial officer - is permissible. It is also permissible to list the languages a particular judicial officer speaks if that judicial officer performs wedding ceremonies free of charge as a service to the public.
